subject: Clarify: session trace retainability and customer-specific CAIQ/SIG evidence
messages:
From: Ian Roberts <ian.roberts@horizonhealth.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Security Team <security@horizonhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Session trace retainability requirements + CAIQ follow-up

Hi Sofia,

Hope you're well. We're progressing through our security review for the pilot and have two related asks: one technical, one for evidence.

1) Session traces / ephemeral inference logs: Our internal policy requires a 30-day retention window for user session traces used for troubleshooting, but some clinical partners require longer (90 days). We're trying to confirm whether Redwood can: a) support tenant-scoped TTLs per account (30 days standard, allow customer-requested 90 days), and b) provide a defensible proof-of-delete when TTLs expire. We also need to understand how key rotation affects proof-of-delete for encrypted logs.

2) SIG/CAIQ evidence: Could you provide your completed SIG answers and any artefacts you can share for the log retention and deletion controls (e.g., retention matrix, proof-of-delete playbook, sampling attestation)? Redaction or pseudo-anonymized samples are fine.

We are aiming to finalize vendor controls by end of next week. Can you let me know feasibility and any follow-up info you need? If useful, we can book a short workshop with your security and infra folks.

Thanks,
Ian Roberts\Lead InfoSec, Horizon Health
Ian Roberts
Ian.Roberts@horizonhealth.ai
+1 415 555 0198

Attachment: Horizon-SIG-Questions-2028.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ian Roberts <ian.roberts@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session trace retainability requirements + CAIQ follow-up

Hi Ian — thanks for the clear ask. We're happy to support the pilot and can provide the SIG/CAIQ artifacts. A few quick notes and requests so we send the right evidence: 

- Tenant-scoped TTLs: Redwood supports per-tenant retention windows in both Hosted and Dedicated modes. For Private (VPC/on‑prem) customers, we provide config templates but the customer controls final TTL enforcement.

- Proof-of-delete: We can provide a proof-of-delete workflow that contains deletion logs, exportable deletion receipts, and sampling attestations. However, when logs are encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, the proof-of-delete semantics change — key destruction / rotation impacts recoverability claims.

- We need to know whether Horizon intends to use our managed KMS or customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM) for the pilot. That will determine the artifacts we deliver.

Action items I propose: 
1) Internal triage (cc'd): Kim/Priyom/Jonas — can you confirm the standard proof-of-delete artifact set we can share and whether we have an existing CAIQ-backed PDF for retention controls?
2) Ian — can you confirm expected deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and whether Horizon will request any tenant-level exceptions to the default 30-day baseline?

I'll coordinate an evidence pack and propose a 30-minute workshop once we have the answers.

Best,
Sofia\Security & Compliance\Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session trace retainability requirements + CAIQ follow-up (internal)

Sofia / team — quick technical notes from infra: 

- Tenant TTLs: Implemented via metadata TTL on the session-trace table and enforced by the retention service. Hosted/Dedicated: we can apply tenant-scoped TTLs centrally. For Private we ship the retention controller and a config file; the customer operator applies it.

- Proof-of-delete: Our standard artifact set is: deletion audit record (timestamp, tenant_id, object_ids deleted), S3/Blob lifecycle event logs, and a signed deletion receipt generated by the retention service (PKI-signed by Redwood). We also provide a sampling export (CSV) showing object_ids removed for attestation purposes.

- KMS / key rotation: If Redwood-managed keys are used, proof-of-delete + key rotation is straightforward: we can show key versions used to encrypt objects and deletion events. If a customer-managed key (CMK/HSM) is used and the customer rotates or truncates keys, we cannot sign a claim about irrecoverability after rotation unless the customer provides key rotation events or revocation proof.

- For a 90-day exception: no architectural blocker. We should document compensating controls (restricted access, additional log masking, and periodic sampling reviews). That helps with SOC2 auditor questions.

Attachments (internal): session-log-retention-matrix.csv — matrix of retention windows, enforcement mechanism, and evidence produced.

Happy to join a workshop; I can present the proof-of-delete flow and the KMS caveats.

— Priyom\Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ian Roberts <ian.roberts@horizonhealth.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session trace retainability requirements + CAIQ follow-up

Ian — following internal confirmation, please find attached a starter evidence pack and the retention matrix. Highlights below: 

- Tenant-scoped TTLs: Supported for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private we provide the controller and documented config. We can support a 90-day tenant exception for Horizon as an opt-in offer. 

- Proof-of-delete package we are sharing: 
  * Redwood-SIG-Answers-Horizon-2028.pdf (completed SIG sections relevant to retention/deletion and references to controls).
  * session-log-retention-matrix.csv (shows enforcement point, artifact type, and sampling guidance).
  * Proof-of-delete playbook (section included in the PDF) with expected deliverables: deletion receipts, sampling exports, and signed audit records.

- KMS note: If Horizon uses customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM), please confirm whether Horizon will provide rotation logs (or accept our hosted KMS). If you require irrevocable deletion semantics via key destruction, we can discuss a KMS plan — but note that key destruction has operational implications and may affect forensic capabilities.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Quick workshop — 30 minutes. Proposed times: Wed 22 Aug 2028 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 23 Aug 2028 14:00–14:30 PT. Priyom will demo the deletion receipts and KMS flow; Kim will cover SOC2 mapping.
2) If you confirm Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and whether you plan to use CMK, we'll finalize the SIG PDF with any redaction and produce the final sampling CSV.

Attachments: Redwood-SIG-Answers-Horizon-2028.pdf (pdf), session-log-retention-matrix.csv (csv)

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova\Security & Compliance\Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
From: Ian Roberts <ian.roberts@horizonhealth.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Security Team <security@horizonhealth.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Session trace retainability requirements + CAIQ follow-up

Sofia — thanks, this is helpful. We'll take the Hosted pilot initially and keep keys with Redwood for simplicity. The 90-day exception will be customer opt-in per tenant — we plan to list affected tenants in the contract SOW.

Workshop: Wed 22 Aug 2028 10:00 PT would have conflicted with our executive review; can we do Thu 23 Aug 2028 14:00 PT? Please send calendar invite.

One small ask before the workshop: can you include an example of a signed deletion receipt (redacted object ids are fine) in the pack so our auditors can see the format? If you can attach that to the invite, it will speed review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Ian
